introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Physics 2 (0780), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2021. Time allowed: two and a half hours.**

Answer ALL questions. Section I is designed to be answered in 1 hour, Section II in 30 minutes and Section III in 1 hour. You are advised to divide your time accordingly. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations you must show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Calculators and formulae booklet are allowed.

**Structure of the paper.** SECTION I (One hour): questions 1 to 5 are compulsory; in question 6 answer EITHER 6 (a), (b) and (c) OR 6 (d), (e) and (f). SECTION II (30 minutes): DATA ANALYSIS, question 7. SECTION III (1 hour): OPTIONS - answer any two questions from the four options (Option 1: Energy resources and environmental physics, question 8; Option 2: Communication, question 9; Option 3: Electronics, question 10; Option 4: Medical physics, question 11).

No data sheet is printed in the paper: whenever a constant is needed, the model answer states the value it uses.
enonce_intro_markdown:
Figure 1 shows how three capacitors are connected in a circuit. One of the capacitors has an unknown capacitance, $X$. Given that the total charge stored on the capacitors is $1500\ \mu\mathrm{C}$ with the switch closed and the potential difference between A and B is $12.0\ \mathrm{V}$.

![fig-1](gce-al-physics-2021-p2-officiel-cameroun_exercice_3_fig_1.png)

figures.legende: Figure 1 : a 12 V battery and a switch feed points A and B. Between A and B there are three branches in parallel: a branch with a 20 microfarad capacitor in series with a 60 microfarad capacitor, a branch with the capacitor X, and a branch with a 150 kilohm resistor.

Question 3, figure 1 : l'association se lit ainsi : 20 microF et 60 microF en série sur une branche, en parallèle avec X, le tout en parallèle avec la résistance de 150 kilohms entre A et B. Cette lecture donne X = 110 microF ; elle est cohérente avec la charge totale imprimée de 1500 microC sous 12,0 V (125 microF). La résistance est supposée connectée en permanence entre A et B (elle assure la décharge en (b)) ; la pile est supposée de résistance interne nulle.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Calculate the

(i) total capacitance in the circuit

(ii) value of $X$

(iii) potential difference across the $60\ \mu\mathrm{F}$ capacitor.
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Reading the circuit.** Between A and B the $20\ \mu\mathrm{F}$ and $60\ \mu\mathrm{F}$ capacitors are **in series** (one branch), and this branch is **in parallel** with $X$. The $150\ \mathrm{k\Omega}$ resistor carries a steady current but stores no charge.

**(i) Total capacitance.**
$$C_T = \frac{Q}{V} = \frac{1500\ \mu\mathrm{C}}{12.0\ \mathrm{V}} = 125\ \mu\mathrm{F}.$$

**(ii) Value of $X$.** The series branch has
$$C_s = \frac{20\times60}{20+60} = \frac{1200}{80} = 15\ \mu\mathrm{F}.$$
Capacitors in parallel add: $C_T = C_s + X$, so
$$X = 125 - 15 = 110\ \mu\mathrm{F}.$$
(Check: charge on $X$ is $110\times12.0 = 1320\ \mu\mathrm{C}$; charge on the series branch is $15\times12.0 = 180\ \mu\mathrm{C}$; total $= 1500\ \mu\mathrm{C}$.)

**(iii) P.d. across the $60\ \mu\mathrm{F}$ capacitor.** The whole series branch is across A and B, so it has $12.0\ \mathrm{V}$ across it, and the charge on the branch (the same on both capacitors in series) is
$$Q = C_sV = 15\ \mu\mathrm{F}\times12.0\ \mathrm{V} = 180\ \mu\mathrm{C}.$$
$$V_{60} = \frac{Q}{C} = \frac{180\ \mu\mathrm{C}}{60\ \mu\mathrm{F}} = 3.0\ \mathrm{V}.$$
(The $20\ \mu\mathrm{F}$ capacitor has $180/20 = 9.0\ \mathrm{V}$, and $3.0 + 9.0 = 12.0\ \mathrm{V}$.)

**Answers:** $C_T = 125\ \mu\mathrm{F}$; $X = 110\ \mu\mathrm{F}$; $V_{60} = 3.0\ \mathrm{V}$.

questions.enonce_markdown: The supply is disconnected and the capacitors discharged through the $150\ \mathrm{k\Omega}$ resistor. Calculate the time taken for the potential difference between A and B to fall to $6.0\ \mathrm{V}$. *[8 marks for question 3]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Once the switch is opened, the three capacitors (total capacitance $C = 125\ \mu\mathrm{F}$ from part (a)) discharge through the $150\ \mathrm{k\Omega}$ resistor, which is connected across A and B.

Time constant:
$$\tau = RC = 150\times10^{3}\ \Omega\times125\times10^{-6}\ \mathrm{F} = 18.75\ \mathrm{s}.$$

The p.d. across the capacitors decays exponentially:
$$V = V_0 e^{-t/RC}.$$

With $V_0 = 12.0\ \mathrm{V}$ and $V = 6.0\ \mathrm{V}$:
$$\frac{6.0}{12.0} = e^{-t/RC} \;\Rightarrow\; \ln 2 = \frac{t}{RC}$$
$$t = RC\ln 2 = 18.75\times0.693 = 13.0\ \mathrm{s}.$$

**The p.d. falls to $6.0\ \mathrm{V}$ after about $13\ \mathrm{s}$** (one half-life of the discharge, $t_{1/2} = 0.693\,RC$).
